mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-45.6 to -36.4 to -28.1 to -28.0), indicating an entrenched recovery momentum in shopping and recreation activity that will continue to push the 4-week mean higher as pent-up demand and habituation to current restriction levels persist.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite three prior weeks of consecutive increase.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved sharply from -52.3 to -36.6 over four weeks. If TRANSIT crosses above -35 and holds for two consecutive weeks, it signals a critical mass of commuters and errand-runners returning to public transit, which mechanically feeds foot traffic into nearby retail and recreation venues within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -35 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -52.3 to -36.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the two weeks following TRANSIT sustaining above -35, or RETAIL_REC falls while TRANSIT remains above that threshold.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stagnated near -37 to -35.9 while TRANSIT has improved by nearly 16 points over the same period, indicating the transit recovery is driven by non-commuting trips (shopping, leisure) rather than work travel. This decoupling predicts continued growth in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as discretionary transit use substitutes for commuting as the main driver.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES changes by less than 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES essentially flat (-37.1 to -35.9) while TRANSIT rose from -52.3 to -36.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining flat and TRANSIT continuing to improve, indicating the decoupling does not translate to retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility turned positive for the first time at t-1w (6.1) and strengthened further to 9.1, signaling a broader population-level shift toward outdoor and leisure activity consistent with a reopening regime. In such a regime, sustained positive PARKS readings co-move with rising RETAIL_REC as the same behavioral loosening that drives park visits also drives shopping and dining trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains positive for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned positive at t-1w and rose to 9.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following two weeks despite PARKS remaining positive for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC falls while PARKS stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued tightly between 7.3 and 7.4 over four weeks, indicating households have settled into a stable routine rather than continuing to shelter more. This behavioral saturation signals no further at-home retrenchment, supporting a modest increase in RETAIL_REC as the marginal population that would further reduce outside trips has already done so.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean varies by less than 0.5 points across four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between 7.3 and 7.4 for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat within the 0.5-point band, indicating saturation does not predict retail direction.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point falls in mid-September, when seasonal cooling and back-to-school/autumn shopping cycles typically shift activity from outdoor parks toward indoor retail venues. Given PARKS has already turned sharply positive while weather-driven seasonality will soon reverse outdoor preference, RETAIL_REC is expected to rise over the next four weeks as seasonal demand migrates indoors.
candidate_trigger: calendar period falls within September-October seasonal transition
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days during the September-October window despite PARKS having peaked and begun to recede.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has decelerated toward baseline (-28.3 to -10.6), a pattern consistent with easing of essential-trip-only policy restrictions. Such policy loosening typically extends to non-essential retail and recreation venues with roughly a one-week lag, so RETAIL_REC is expected to rise over the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM moves within -15 to 0 band for the most recent week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -28.3 to -10.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following GROCERY_PHARM entering the -15 to 0 band, or continues to decline despite grocery normalization.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC has collapsed from +9.2 points (t-2w to t-1w) to +0.1 points (t-1w to t-0w), while TRANSIT remains deeply negative at -36.6. This stalling of retail recovery alongside persistently suppressed transit suggests mobility constraints are capping further retail gains, predicting flat-to-negative RETAIL_REC movement over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change falls below 2 points while TRANSIT remains below -30
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gain fell from +9.2 to +0.1 points while TRANSIT stayed at -36.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite the simultaneous stall in weekly gains and persistently low TRANSIT, invalidating the capping mechanism.
